text:
rachel: heads-up: reproduced an OOM pattern on Dedicated during our micro-batch PERF run. p95 jumps and alloc failures after ~10k small requests. gist with reproducer & heap: https://gist.github.com/foo/microalloc-repro.sh
dia: can you paste the short allocator/evictor snippet? trying to see whether offload quota or fragmentation
rachel: logs: 
```
[2026-03-26T07:18:10Z] evictor: staging_used=1018MB staging_limit=1024MB
[2026-03-26T07:18:10Z] evictor: offload_reject=23 reason=reserve_exhausted
[2026-03-26T07:18:11Z] allocator: alloc transient_fail size=48KB tenant=svc-ingest
[2026-03-26T07:18:12Z] allocator: tiny_slab_frag=78%
```

tom: pattern looks like reserve exhaustion + high tiny-slab fragmentation. small KV caches keep allocating and never hit hotness to be promoted/offloaded
yusuf: are we still using alloc(size) -> handle only on the fast path? i thought we added a hotness hint in the last release but maybe it's opt-in and not used by caller code
dia: fast path is still alloc(size) only. the residency hint is a separate async call. that's the culprit here: caller workload creates then immediate work with the buffer before hint lands
claire: proposal: add a tiny atomic_reserve_for_request(req_id, expected_bytes) that vends a short-lived reserve token and reduces allocation failures for micro-bursts. combine with alloc(size, opts) where opts includes reserve_token and offloadable_hint
yusuf: +1. design note: make reserve cheap (single atomic decrement on pool counter) and auto-expire after N ms if unused. callers obtain token at request start and consume it lazily at alloc time
rachel: alternate immediate mitigation: increase staging_limit by 8% on Dedicated pools and reduce tiny_slab_pin_priority for 0-64KB allocations so they're easier to evict
tom: long-term: tiny-allocator redesign: subpage=4KB superpage=2MB, maintain freelist of contiguous subpage runs; track per-run owner so coalescing is O(1). reclamation can steal entire superpage runs instead of hunting tiny fragments
dia: metadata format: propose a compact 12-byte inline header for tiny allocations: 1B class, 1B flags, 2B size_code, 4B owner_id, 4B timestamp_bucket -> allows in-place queries for offloadability without external map
yusuf: tradeoff: header increases fragmentation overhead for very small allocs. but we avoid global lookup hot-path which is expensive under scale
claire: telemetry: add metric micro_reserve_stolen, micro_reserve_timeout_ms, alloc_fail_rate_by_bin, tiny_run_coalesce_events. Also histogram per-alloc lifetime by size binachel: rollout plan: emergency config change -> canary dedicated-pool-3 -> watch staging_used, offload_reject, alloc_fail_rate_by_bin for 1h -> if passes, roll. then follow with a small runtime patch to accept reserve tokens in alloc API
infra-bot: deploy: dedicated-2026-03-26T06:50 rolled runtime v2.15.0 (evictor backpressure tuning)
tom: tests: add integration that spawns 500 concurrent micro-requests each doing handful of 8-64KB allocs and asserts no alloc_fail and reserve_token latency < 2ms
dia: logging improvement: when offload_reject occurs include reserve_pool_epoch and per-tenant reserve_usage to speed triage
yusuf: also add a debug-only trace that emits tiny_run_map snapshot when tiny_slab_frag > 70%
claire: RFC checklist: - API: alloc(size, opts) + atomic_reserve API - tiny-allocator internals + superpage compaction algorithm - header layout + tradeoffs - telemetry contract + dashboards - test matrix (unit + perf rig)
rachel: i'll open emergency PR (config bump + lower pin priority) and start RFC draft for the allocator+reserve. tagging @tom @dia for review. infra-bot: created INC-2026-502 (microalloc reserve exhaustion on Dedicated)
omitting: title as per slack docs
